narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Tells the story and introduces each speech.

the-lord.name: The Lord
the-lord.note: God, answering Job out of the whirlwind and judging the friends.

1.t: And the Lord answering Job out of the whirlwind, said:

2.t: Gird up thy loins like a man: I will ask thee, and do thou tell me.

3.t: Wilt thou make void my judgment: and condemn me, that thou mayst be justified?

4.t: And hast thou an arm like God, and canst thou thunder with a voice like him?

5.t: Clothe thyself with beauty, and set thyself up on high, and be glorious, and put on goodly garments.

6.t: Scatter the proud in thy indignation, and behold every arrogant man, and humble him.

7.t: Look on all that are proud, and confound them, and crush the wicked in their place,

8.t: Hide them in the dust together, and plunge their faces into the pit.

9.t: Then I will confess that thy right hand is able to save thee.

10.t: Behold behemoth whom I made with thee, he eateth grass like an ox.

11.t: His strength is in his loins, and his force in the navel of his belly.

12.t: He setteth up his tail like a cedar, the sinews of his testicles are wrapped together.

13.t: His bones are like pipes of brass, his gristle like plates of iron.

14.t: He is the beginning of the ways of God, who made him, he will apply his sword.

15.t: To him the mountains bring forth grass: there all the beasts of the field shall play.

16.t: He sleepeth under the shadow, in the covert of the reed, and in moist places.

17.t: The shades cover his shadow, the willows of the brook shall compass him about.

18.t: Behold, he will drink up a river, and not wonder: and he trusteth that the Jordan may run into his mouth.

19.t: In his eyes as with a hook he shall take him, and bore through his nostrils with stakes.

20.t: Canst thou draw out the leviathan with a hook, or canst thou tie his tongue with a cord?

21.t: Canst thou put a ring in his nose, or bore through his jaw with a buckle?

22.t: Will he make many supplications to thee, or speak soft words to thee?

23.t: Will he make a covenant with thee, and wilt thou take him to be a servant for ever?

24.t: Shalt thou play with him as with a bird, or tie him up for thy handmaids?

25.t: Shall friends cut him in pieces, shall merchants divide him?

26.t: Wilt thou fill nets with his skin, and the cabins of fishes with his head?

27.t: Lay thy hand upon him: remember the battle, and speak no more.

28.t: Behold his hope shall fail him, and in the sight of all he shall be cast down.
